items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: Miss Ethel told my mother, “My name is James Richard,” she said, “Ruby James Richard is down there. He’d be gambling with the guys.”

ctx.x: Was there any conflict between the church music and the religion and the secular blues that you were getting so fond of?

Oh yeah, yeah. They were — there wasn’t a strong conflict because — I’m going to tell this and then, you know in my neighborhood we had everything. When I say everything — on our street there was — three doors down there was people selling what we call hot clothes. You know, suits and everything, that people had shoplifted out of the stores and everything and, but deacons and, you know, all kinds of people would come there and they were religious people, you’d see them at church with that suit on and they got it…

and she said, “You know the reason I left from under the hill, Ethel told me James Richard was down there with the guys gambling.” And when we would gamble we would get a pint of corn whiskey that we knew where the guy who — we wouldn’t do that, we’d get a pint of corn whiskey and but I never drank because I knew my mother could smell it on me and so, but she found me one day gambling. Well she must have came home early. And she never told me. She said, then I said, “When I saw James Richard down there gambling…
